_note: Reported news for the PDF. Compiled every Sunday from the climate-news monitor sources (Eye Radio, Radio Tamazuj, Sudans Post, UN/UNMISS, ReliefWeb, Radio Yei, others); last compiled 2026-10-11. 'counties' lists every county the item names; items with no county go in scope 'national' (state or countrywide). Items older than NEWS_DAYS (21) are dropped.

items.text: No Ebola case has been confirmed in South Sudan; the health system is on high alert after Kenya confirmed its first case (the patient died on 5 October) and with a large outbreak in DR Congo.

Ministry of Water Resources and Irrigation warns of possible Nile flooding, including in and around Juba: simulations suggest Lake Victoria could rise above its historical maximum, and ICPAC sees a higher El Nino likelihood with above-normal rain over the lake basin. Readings from Nimule to Renk and Nasir to Bentiu are falling and below alert levels. Reduced June-September rainfall has also affected several states, including Abyei, Pibor and Ruweng.

Heavy rains and insecurity have left Ibba communities more isolated: the roughly 100 km Yambio-Ibba road is almost impassable (deep potholes, mud and flooding), slowing vehicles to almost walking pace.

UNMISS says flooding has submerged about 70% of the land around Bentiu; about 300,000 people shelter behind dykes held by UNMISS and IOM, and a breach not repaired within ten hours could submerge 50,000. IOM faces a shortfall for dyke maintenance and pumping; heavier rain is expected with El Nino from October to February (county inferred from Bentiu).
Lakes State peace committee (Rumbek) was restructured as heavy rains and flooding raise fears of renewed communal violence and cattle-camp moves; no flood damage reported (county not stated).

UNMISS-backed peace dialogue in Maban discussed flooding and drought as climate shocks; a paramount chief said the prolonged lack of rain is hurting communities more than ever this year. Early warning and evacuation planning were discussed (no figures given).

State health officials report 40 hepatitis E cases, no deaths, over two weeks in Northern Bahr el Ghazal (counties including Aweil East, Aweil North, Gok Machar and Aweil West), which they link to water contaminated during the rains.
Flash flood from heavy overnight rain submerged the Kapuri bridge and stranded travellers on both sides between Kapuri and Juba (county inferred from location).

Heavy rain flooded several IDP camps and damaged makeshift shelters; the relief commission says families in 15 camps across three payams struggle to get food and basic aid, and residents report no medicines and high food prices.
UNMISS says heavy rain, El Nino and funding shortfalls are straining the temporary dykes kept by IOM and UNMISS at Bentiu (county inferred from Bentiu).
Seven-day cholera vaccination drive with MSF and WHO targets more than 100,000 IDPs after thousands of cases in Unity State this year.

State officials, citing a rapid assessment, say about 1.1 million people are affected by a prolonged rainfall deficit across five counties (not named); they fear more hunger later this year and into 2027.

Water Resources Minister says Uganda's notice expects record Lake Victoria levels and higher releases into the Nile, flagging Juba and low-lying areas for severe riverine flooding; Nile readings from Nimule to Renk are below alert levels but expected to change quickly.
